bibl.title: Neural Correlate Differences in Number Sense Between Children With Low and Middle/High Socioeconomic Status

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: at which stage of numerical magnitude comparison the processing of children from low and from middle-to-high socioeconomic backgrounds diverges
span.quote: Although some cognitive studies provided reasons that children with low socioeconomic status (SES) showed poor mathematical achievements, there was no explicit evidence to directly explain the root of lagged performance in children with low SES. Therefore, the present study explored the differences in neural correlates in the process of symbolic magnitude comparison between children with different SESs by the event-related potentials (ERPs).

span.label: whether socioeconomic status affects the early attentional stages of symbolic number comparison, the later representational stage, or both
span.quote: this study proposed the first hypothesis that children with different SES would show variation in the early recognition stage of digit stimuli. In addition, since children with low SES often lag significantly behind in mathematical learning, this study assumed that in the second phase of numerical comparison, children with low SES would show a significant difference from those with middle–high SES. However, previous studies did not find a significant difference on P3b between children with different SES (i.e., Kishiyama et al., 2008 ), so we believed that in the magnitude comparison task, children with different SES would not show significant difference in this late component, which is dependent on the integrity of the temporal–parietal cortex.

span.label: reports amplitude differences between SES groups in two early frontal components and none in the late parietal component, with no accompanying behavioural difference
span.quote: According to the results of anterior N1 (early attention) and P2 (extraction of numerical meaning) over the frontal region, the differences among children with different SESs were manifested as differences in general neural activities in terms of attention and top-down cognitive control.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The results of the present study provided evidence that there were neural correlate differences between children with different SESs.

span.label: symbolic numerical magnitude comparison
span.quote: Therefore, the present study explored the differences in neural correlates in the process of symbolic magnitude comparison between children with different SESs by the event-related potentials (ERPs).

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: According to the selection paradigm ( Moyer and Landauer, 1967 ), the magnitude comparison task was presented to each participant with two single digits displayed simultaneously during the recording session.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: low-SES children must invest extra attentional resources to suppress interference from irrelevant information in order to reach the same performance, which shows up as a larger (more negative) anterior N1
span.quote: The present study confirmed the conclusion that children with low SES showed more negative amplitude between 100 and 140 ms after the digits occurred, indicating that when these children perceived and recognized the numbers, they needed to invest more attention resources to suppress the interference of irrelevant information to their intentional attention to catch up with children with middle/high SES.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: chronic family stressors raise basal corticosteroid levels, which degrades selective attention and shapes the long postnatal development of the prefrontal cortex
span.quote: They are exposed to more chronic stressors in the family, such as prolonged poverty and parental strife, and therefore have higher basal levels of the stress hormone corticosteroids and poorer selective attention

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SES acts as a distal environmental factor that reaches the early prefrontal control stage but not the deep parietal numerical representation stage
span.quote: Therefore, as a distal factor, SES is not enough to affect the deep numerical processing in the parietal lobe.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: numbers close together overlap more on the mental number line, making them harder to discriminate, which produces the distance effect
span.quote: When the to-be-compared numbers were close to each other, more greater overlapping areas of these two numbers on the mental number line would make it more difficult to distinguish one from the other.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a ceiling effect on an easy task hides the group difference at the behavioural level while ERPs still reveal it
span.quote: One reason is that the experimental task is relatively easy for second-graders (in the second semester), so the “ceiling effect” appears.

span.label: the proposed route is attentional: low-SES children are said to spend more resources suppressing irrelevant information to reach the same performance
span.quote: The present study confirmed the conclusion that children with low SES showed more negative amplitude between 100 and 140 ms after the digits occurred, indicating that when these children perceived and recognized the numbers, they needed to invest more attention resources to suppress the interference of irrelevant information to their intentional attention to catch up with children with middle/high SES.

span.label: prefrontal cortex develops slowly after birth, which is offered as why an environmental variable could reach it
span.quote: Human’s prefrontal cortex has a long period of postnatal development (e.g., Casey et al., 2000 ; Fuster, 2002 ), so the external environment, such as environmental deprivation and stress ( Braun et al., 2000 ) and environmental complexity ( van Praag et al., 2000 ), will affect the development of the prefrontal cortex.

span.label: two candidate environmental routes are named: impoverished cognitive input, and chronic stress raising corticosteroids
span.quote: In addition, these children from L-SES families often experience higher levels of stress. They are exposed to more chronic stressors in the family, such as prolonged poverty and parental strife, and therefore have higher basal levels of the stress hormone corticosteroids and poorer selective attention

span.label: the distance effect is read as overlap on a mental number line, closer numbers overlapping more
span.quote: These findings indicate that there exists a “mental number line” for children in the process of numerical comparison. Children might judge the magnitudes according to the to-be-compared number’s position on this mental number line. When the to-be-compared numbers were close to each other, more greater overlapping areas of these two numbers on the mental number line would make it more difficult to distinguish one from the other. Conversely, it was much easier to compare two numbers when they were more distant from each other.

span.label: the temporal order of the components is mapped onto a front-to-back anatomical order, control before representation
span.quote: Previous studies have found that prefrontal cortex activation comes first compared with parietal cortex during arithmetic processing ( Menon et al., 2000 ; Brass et al., 2005 ). The anterior component is related to the cognitive control processing of the prefrontal cortex, while the parietal component reflects the involvement of numerical representation

span.label: The comparison task was too easy for the age group, producing a ceiling effect that may hide behavioural SES differences.
span.note: what this limits: the absence of a behavioural SES difference: THE EXPERIMENTAL TASK IS RELATIVELY EASY FOR SECOND-GRADERS ... SO THE 'CEILING EFFECT' APPEARS
span.quote: One reason is that the experimental task is relatively easy for second-graders (in the second semester), so the “ceiling effect” appears.

span.label: The expected DE did not appear in the late time window, possibly because of the specific task used.
span.note: what this limits: the null in the late time window: it MAY BE DUE TO THE DIFFERENCES IN THE EXPERIMENTAL TASKS
span.quote: However, in the present study, children with different SESs did not show a numerical DE on the average amplitude in this time window, which may be due to the differences in the experimental tasks.

span.label: The 'high SES' group is only middle-to-high in absolute terms, because the sampling city is economically less developed.
span.note: what this limits: what the group label means: A HIGH SCORE ON THE SES QUESTIONNAIRE ONLY REPRESENTED A MIDDLE TO HIGH LEVEL OF SES
span.quote: Thus in this study, a high score on the SES questionnaire only represented a middle to high level of SES.

span.label: no behavioural difference between the groups; the paper attributes this to a ceiling effect on an easy task
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the numbers: RT 685.63 ms versus 711.16 ms and ACC 95.15% versus 93.19% - EXTREMELY MINOR DIFFERENCES on a task at ceiling
span.quote: Nevertheless, children in different SES groups showed extremely minor differences in RT and ACC on the magnitude comparison task (RT: 685.63 ms for M/H-SES, 711.16 ms for L-SES; ACC: 95.15% for M/H-SES, 93.19% for L-SES). One reason is that the experimental task is relatively easy for second-graders (in the second semester), so the “ceiling effect” appears.

span.label: 52 children were recruited and 32 analysed, after dropout and trial-count exclusions
span.note: what this limits: the sample every effect rests on: INITIALLY, 52 CHILDREN PARTICIPATED ... DATA OF 20 CHILDREN WERE DISCARDED, for dropout, discomfort, movement and insufficient trials
span.quote: Initially, 52 children participated in the study. Before EEG data processing, data of 20 children were discarded, among them 11 children failed to complete the experiment (8 of them dropped out of the experiment early due to a cold or physical discomfort, and 3 other children did not complete the experiment due to constant body shaking, talking, and random responses during the experiment), and 9 children’s sufficient trials were less than 70% of the total after the artifact rejection. Finally, data of 32 children were regarded as valid for the analysis: 16 of them were from the low-SES (L-SES) group (8 girls), and the remaining 16 were from the middle/high-SES (M/H-SES) group (8 girls).

span.label: analysis time windows and electrodes were chosen partly from observation of the data
span.note: what this limits: the statistical strength of every reported component: TIME WINDOWS AND THE ELECTRODES FOR ANALYSIS WERE SELECTED BASED ON PREVIOUS STUDIES AND OBSERVATION RESULTS OF THE DATA
span.quote: Time windows and the electrodes for analysis were selected based on previous studies and observation results of the data.

span.label: high SES here is high only relative to a poor inland city, so the label does not transfer
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, with the reason: the city HAD A RELATIVELY BACKWARD LEVEL OF ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, so the label does not transfer to another sampling frame
span.quote: The participants came from Yinchuan, an inland city in the northwest region of China, which had a relatively backward level of economic development. Thus in this study, a high score on the SES questionnaire only represented a middle to high level of SES.

span.label: the expected DE did not appear on the late component, which the authors attribute to task form and leave for future work
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with the remedy named: IT IS NECESSARY TO COMPARE THE ERP RESULTS WITH DIFFERENT FORMS OF MAGNITUDE COMPARISON TASKS IN THE FUTURE
span.quote: However, in the present study, children with different SESs did not show a numerical DE on the average amplitude in this time window, which may be due to the differences in the experimental tasks. For this reason, it is necessary to compare the ERP results with different forms of magnitude comparison tasks in the future.

span.label: the PISA socioeconomic questionnaire, adapted as the grouping variable
span.quote: The SES criteria consisted of parental education, occupation, and family resources, which together represented SES better than any of these alone

span.label: the distance effect from Moyer and Landauer's reaction-time paradigm, used here as the task manipulation
span.quote: Moyer and Landauer (1967) were the first to measure the RT in a selection paradigm by pressing the associated button. They found that participants made more mistakes and required more time when the two numbers to be compared were close (e.g., 7 vs. 9) than farther apart (e.g., 2 vs. 9). That is, there is a distance effect (DE) in the process of numerical comparison.

span.label: number sense has no agreed definition - the paper opens by saying cognitive psychologists and math educators define it differently, then adopts a six-part working list
span.quote: Although cognitive psychologists and math educators have different definitions of number sense ( Gersten et al., 2005 ), most of them agree that it is an ability to subitize small quantities, discern number patterns, compare numerical magnitudes, estimate quantities, count, and perform simple number transformations

span.label: P2 and P2p are DIFFERENT components separated in time and space, despite names differing by one letter; P2p indexes the DE and P2 does not
span.quote: The next positive wave, P2p, was initially described by Dehaene (1996) as reflecting the DE (right parietal–occipital–temporal positive waveform to close numbers compared to far numbers) and was seen as an index of the approximate magnitude representation ( Hyde and Spelke, 2011 ). This component, simultaneous with N1, is clearly separated in time and space from the earlier broad fronto-central positivity wave, which is classically known as P2

span.label: anterior N1 and posterior N1 are different components with different generators; this study evokes the anterior one where the cited precedent evoked the posterior
span.quote: According to the time and brain regions of occurrence, this component was the anterior N1. This result was inconsistent with a previous study (i.e., Dehaene, 1996 ) in which the posterior N1 was evoked by the number comparison task.

span.label: LPC may or may not be the P3b - the identification is attributed to some researchers and not settled here
span.quote: The last positive component is the late positive component (LPC), which is characterized by later onset (usually after 300 ms) and central–parietal distribution ( Friedman and Johnson, 2000 ). Some researchers suggested that this component was the P3b, which indicated the amount of context updating and also reflected the DE

span.label: SES is a composite score built from parental education, occupation and household resources by item response theory and principal components, not a single measured quantity
span.quote: The SES criteria consisted of parental education, occupation, and family resources, which together represented SES better than any of these alone

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: existence — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: According to the results of anterior N1 (early attention) and P2 (extraction of numerical meaning) over the frontal region, the differences among children with different SESs were manifested as differences in general neural activities in terms of attention and top-down cognitive control.

span.label: method: event-related potentials during a two-digit selection task, comparing 16 low-SES with 16 middle/high-SES children matched on nonverbal and verbal ability
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: According to the selection paradigm ( Moyer and Landauer, 1967 ), the magnitude comparison task was presented to each participant with two single digits displayed simultaneously during the recording session. The stimuli of this task consisted of 10 pairs of Arabic numerals from 1 to 9 (except number “5”), with no repeating digits in each pair (e.g., “3 3”). They were displayed in white Arial font in the center of the computer screen with black background. There were two different numerical distances: 5 (i.e., 1–6, 2–7, 3–8, 4–9) and 1 (i.e., 1–2, 2–3, 3–4, 6–7, 7–8, 8–9). The position where the two numbers appeared was counterbalanced, half on the left and half on the right. There were three blocks of 48 stimuli (144 trials in total; 72 trials per distance condition). The participants were required to decide which of the two numbers was larger by pressing the button on the corresponding side as quickly and accurately as possible.

span.label: phenomenon: symbolic magnitude comparison and the distance effect in second-grade children
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: symbolic numerical magnitude comparison — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Moyer and Landauer (1967) were the first to measure the RT in a selection paradigm by pressing the associated button. They found that participants made more mistakes and required more time when the two numbers to be compared were close (e.g., 7 vs. 9) than farther apart (e.g., 2 vs. 9). That is, there is a distance effect (DE) in the process of numerical comparison.

span.label: replicates → Kishiyama et al., 2008
span.quote: In the present study, an ERP difference among children with different SESs did not appear in the average amplitude of LPC (in the 450–700 ms time window), which was consistent with a previous study (i.e., Kishiyama et al., 2008 ).

span.label: contradicts → Dehaene, 1996
span.quote: This result was inconsistent with a previous study (i.e., Dehaene, 1996 ) in which the posterior N1 was evoked by the number comparison task.

span.label: replicates → Soltész et al., 2007; Gebuis et al., 2009
span.quote: Based on the behavioral data of RT and ACC, second-grade children showed a numerical DE where they judged the numbers with large distance much faster and more accurately, which was consistent with previous studies (e.g., Soltész et al., 2007 ; Gebuis et al., 2009 ).

span.label: contradicts → posterior N1 account of numerical comparison (Dehaene, 1996; Gómez-Velázquez et al., 2015)
span.quote: In this study, the N1 component appeared in the frontal and central regions.

span.label: confirms → Kishiyama et al. 2008, on prefrontal attentional differences by SES and on the absence of a late-component difference
span.quote: In the late stage of cognitive processing, there was no significant difference in the average amplitude of the late positive component (LPC) between children with different SES, indicating that low SES did not influence the information encoding and memory updating of numerical representation, which was responsible by the parietal lobe.

span.label: contradicts → Dehaene 1996, in which numerical comparison evoked a posterior rather than an anterior N1
span.quote: According to the time and brain regions of occurrence, this component was the anterior N1. This result was inconsistent with a previous study (i.e., Dehaene, 1996 ) in which the posterior N1 was evoked by the number comparison task.

span.label: reconciles → that discrepancy, by attributing it to one digit against a fixed baseline versus two digits presented together
span.quote: The reasons that the N1 component is evoked in different brain regions are because of the differences in the form of the stimulus presentation and in the comparison baseline between different experiments. In previous studies (e.g., Dehaene, 1996 ; Gómez-Velázquez et al., 2015 ), the classification paradigm was used to explore the process of numerical comparison. In this task, only one digit was presented in each trial, without changing the baseline number to be compared (e.g., “5”). In the present study, each trial of the task included two digits simultaneously (e.g., “2” and “7”). As a result, participants firstly needed to accurately represent each number on their mental number line, instead of making classification judgments based on a reference point.

span.label: distinguishes-from → children with mathematical learning disability, whose parietal processing is impaired
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER PARIETAL NUMBER PROCESSING IS IMPAIRED. 'fMRI studies found that CHILDREN WITH MLD HAD IMPAIRMENT IN THE BILATERAL INTRAPARIETAL SULCUS (IPS) INVOLVED IN NUMBER MAGNITUDE PROCESSING, and had significant differences in the P300 latency and amplitude compared to normal children.' The comparison group is defined by a deficit in a specific region and function, so a result about `low number sense` does not transfer to it without that. Q-495.
span.quote: Although fMRI studies found that children with MLD had impairment in the bilateral intraparietal sulcus (IPS) involved in number magnitude processing ( Habib, 2000 ; Mussolin et al., 2014 ), and had significant differences in the P300 latency and amplitude compared to normal children ( Soltész et al., 2007 ; Taylor and Keenan, 2010 ; Wang et al., 2015 ), in this study, children with L-SES were not MLD, and some of them even had higher math scores in the class. Therefore, as a distal factor, SES is not enough to affect the deep numerical processing in the parietal lobe.

span.label: extends → behavioural SES research on number line estimation and calculation, by moving to symbolic magnitude comparison
span.quote: Although some cognitive studies provided reasons that children with low socioeconomic status (SES) showed poor mathematical achievements, there was no explicit evidence to directly explain the root of lagged performance in children with low SES. Therefore, the present study explored the differences in neural correlates in the process of symbolic magnitude comparison between children with different SESs by the event-related potentials (ERPs).

span.label: P2 —distinct-from→ P2p
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: separated in time and in scalp location, and only P2p carries the DE. Names differing by one letter for two different things - the fast-ripples pattern again
span.quote: The next positive wave, P2p, was initially described by Dehaene (1996) as reflecting the DE (right parietal–occipital–temporal positive waveform to close numbers compared to far numbers) and was seen as an index of the approximate magnitude representation ( Hyde and Spelke, 2011 ). This component, simultaneous with N1, is clearly separated in time and space from the earlier broad fronto-central positivity wave, which is classically known as P2

span.label: anterior N1 —distinct-from→ posterior N1
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: different scalp regions and different generators. The same label N1 names whichever one a given paradigm evokes
span.quote: According to the time and brain regions of occurrence, this component was the anterior N1. This result was inconsistent with a previous study (i.e., Dehaene, 1996 ) in which the posterior N1 was evoked by the number comparison task.

span.label: LPC —same-as→ P3b
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — an identity ATTRIBUTED to some researchers and not adopted by this paper; weight deliberately low Q-558, 2026-08-15: READ THIS EDGE WITH senses[3]: the sense on this record that quotes the SAME SENTENCE says the identification is not settled: 'LPC may or may not be the P3b - the identification is attributed to some researchers and not settled here'. This edge asserts an identity the paper declines to assert. The type is left as it stands pending the wider decision about what `same-as` asserts; this note exists so the two are read together.
span.quote: The last positive component is the late positive component (LPC), which is characterized by later onset (usually after 300 ms) and central–parietal distribution ( Friedman and Johnson, 2000 ). Some researchers suggested that this component was the P3b, which indicated the amount of context updating and also reflected the DE

span.label: socioeconomic status —distinct-from→ Raven
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — the matching null that licenses reading the ERP difference as SES rather than ability - and it is marginal, t(30) = -1.96 with CI [-7.41, 0.16]
span.quote: There was no significant difference in the scores in general cognitive ability (R’SPM-CR: L-SES M = 37.00, SD = 5.92; M/H-SES M = 40.63, SD = 4.46, t (30) = −1.96, p > 0.05, 95% CI = [−7.41, 0.16]) and verbal intelligence (MSCA-CR: L-SES M = 77.06, SD = 9.77; M/H-SES M = 80.56, SD = 5.61, t (30) = −1.24, p > 0.05, 95% CI = [−9.25, 2.25]) between the two SES groups.

span.label: distance effect —operationalised-as→ mental number line
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — direction is observation-to-construct: the behavioural effect is read as evidence for the representation
span.quote: These findings indicate that there exists a “mental number line” for children in the process of numerical comparison. Children might judge the magnitudes according to the to-be-compared number’s position on this mental number line. When the to-be-compared numbers were close to each other, more greater overlapping areas of these two numbers on the mental number line would make it more difficult to distinguish one from the other. Conversely, it was much easier to compare two numbers when they were more distant from each other.

span.label: magnitude comparison —part-of→ number sense
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Although cognitive psychologists and math educators have different definitions of number sense ( Gersten et al., 2005 ), most of them agree that it is an ability to subitize small quantities, discern number patterns, compare numerical magnitudes, estimate quantities, count, and perform simple number transformations

span.label: anterior N1 —operationalised-as→ top-down cognitive control
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the amplitude is read as attentional effort; the interpretation is imported from prior work rather than tested here
span.quote: The present study confirmed the conclusion that children with low SES showed more negative amplitude between 100 and 140 ms after the digits occurred, indicating that when these children perceived and recognized the numbers, they needed to invest more attention resources to suppress the interference of irrelevant information to their intentional attention to catch up with children with middle/high SES.

span.label: LPC —operationalised-as→ parietal lobe
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — scalp component assigned to a region by convention, which is what makes the null a claim about the parietal lobe
span.quote: In the late stage of cognitive processing (450–700 ms), there was no significant difference in the average amplitude of the LPC among children with different SES, indicating that low SES did not influence information encoding and memory updating of numerical representation, which was responsible by the parietal lobe.

span.label: ceiling effect —causes→ magnitude comparison
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — offered after the fact to explain why no behavioural difference accompanies the neural one
span.quote: Nevertheless, children in different SES groups showed extremely minor differences in RT and ACC on the magnitude comparison task (RT: 685.63 ms for M/H-SES, 711.16 ms for L-SES; ACC: 95.15% for M/H-SES, 93.19% for L-SES). One reason is that the experimental task is relatively easy for second-graders (in the second semester), so the “ceiling effect” appears.

span.label: socioeconomic status —distinct-from→ MLD
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: the low-SES children were not clinically impaired and some scored highly, so the parietal null is not a null about impairment
span.quote: Although fMRI studies found that children with MLD had impairment in the bilateral intraparietal sulcus (IPS) involved in number magnitude processing ( Habib, 2000 ; Mussolin et al., 2014 ), and had significant differences in the P300 latency and amplitude compared to normal children ( Soltész et al., 2007 ; Taylor and Keenan, 2010 ; Wang et al., 2015 ), in this study, children with L-SES were not MLD, and some of them even had higher math scores in the class. Therefore, as a distal factor, SES is not enough to affect the deep numerical processing in the parietal lobe.

span.label: corticosteroids —causes→ top-down cognitive control
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — a mechanism cited from other literature, not measured here
span.quote: In addition, these children from L-SES families often experience higher levels of stress. They are exposed to more chronic stressors in the family, such as prolonged poverty and parental strife, and therefore have higher basal levels of the stress hormone corticosteroids and poorer selective attention

span.label: repeated-measures ANOVA
span.quote: For the behavioral data (RT and ACC), to explore the differences in DE between the two SES groups, an SES (L-SES vs. M/H-SES) × numerical distance (large vs. small) repeated-measures ANOVA was conducted.

span.label: Greenhouse-Geisser correction for sphericity
span.quote: In the present study, Greenhouse–Geisser correction was performed in all behavioral and physiological ANOVAs as necessary.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: There was a significant difference in the years of education between the two groups [ t (26) = 13.21, p < 0.001].

span.label: correlation (test-retest reliability)
span.quote: The results showed that the task was extremely reliable for both RT ( r = 0.97, p < 0.001) and ACC ( r = 0.81, p < 0.001), suggesting good task reliability

span.label: post hoc test
span.quote: A post hoc test revealed that the amplitudes in frontal and fronto-central regions were significantly larger than that in the central region

span.label: effect size (partial eta squared)
span.quote: A significant main effect of numerical distance was found [ F (1,30) = 120.95, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0.801], suggesting that RT for the small distance was significantly longer than that for the large distance.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Then, a main component analysis was conducted, and the following formula was used to obtain the SES score:

span.label: item response theory parameter estimation
span.quote: utilizing the Item Response Theory to perform parameter estimation on family resources, in which the parameter estimation index is acquired;

span.label: repeated-measurement ANOVA
span.quote: The results showed that the SES main effect was significant, revealing that children with L-SES showed more negative amplitude than the children with M/H-SES [ F (1,30) = 12.85, p < 0.01, η p 2 = 0.300]

span.label: Greenhouse–Geisser correction
span.quote: Finally, to explore the time course of magnitude comparison of the children with different SESs, three components were selected: the anterior N1 (100–140 ms, F3/FZ/F4/FC3/FCZ/FC4/C3/CZ/C4) ( Kong et al., 1999 ; Yagoubi et al., 2003 ; Kishiyama et al., 2008 ), the P2 component (200–250 ms, F3/FZ/F4/FC3/FCZ/FC4/C3/CZ/C4) ( Szücs and Csépe, 2004 ; Chen et al., 2013 ), and the LPC (450–700 ms, F3/FZ/F4, C3/CZ/C4, P3/PZ/P4)

span.label: partial eta squared
span.quote: In the 450–700 ms time window, an SES (2) × numerical distance (2) × location (3) repeated-measurement ANOVA was performed. The results indicated that the SES main effect was not significant [ F (1,30) = 1.18, p > 0.05, η p 2 = 0.038].

span.label: 95% CI
span.quote: There was no significant difference in the scores in general cognitive ability (R’SPM-CR: L-SES M = 37.00, SD = 5.92; M/H-SES M = 40.63, SD = 4.46, t (30) = −1.96, p > 0.05, 95% CI = [−7.41, 0.16]) and verbal intelligence (MSCA-CR: L-SES M = 77.06, SD = 9.77; M/H-SES M = 80.56, SD = 5.61, t (30) = −1.24, p > 0.05, 95% CI = [−9.25, 2.25]) between the two SES groups.

span.label: correlation analysis
span.quote: The current study conducted a correlation analysis to explore the test–retest reliabilities in RT and ACC between the first- and second-half trials of the experimental task. The results showed that the task was extremely reliable for both RT ( r = 0.97, p < 0.001) and ACC ( r = 0.81, p < 0.001), suggesting good task reliability

span.label: Low-SES and middle/high-SES second-graders did not differ behaviourally on the symbolic magnitude comparison task, in either reaction time or accuracy.
span.quote: However, there was no significant difference in the behavioral indices of the magnitude comparison task between children with different SESs.

span.label: Both SES groups showed the classic numerical DE, responding faster and more accurately to number pairs that were far apart.
span.quote: The behavioral results suggested that the DE existed in both groups; that is, children were faster and more accurate when judging numbers with large distance compared with the small distance.

span.label: In the earliest window (100-140 ms) the anterior N1 was more negative in low-SES children, indicating an early attentional difference despite equal behaviour.
span.quote: The results showed that the SES main effect was significant, revealing that children with L-SES showed more negative amplitude than the children with M/H-SES

span.label: In the 200-250 ms window the frontal P2 was more positive in middle/high-SES children, indicating a difference in extraction of numerical meaning and early semantic processing.
span.quote: revealed that the SES main effect was significant, suggesting that the children with M/H-SES showed more positive amplitude than their counterparts

span.label: The late positive component showed no SES difference, so the late parietal stage of numerical representation appears unaffected by low SES.

span.quote: The findings in this study provide some valuable suggestions to researchers and educators about the mathematical education of children with low SES. It is insufficient and unscientific to only provide children with low SES with books and toys. Teachers and tutors should pay more attention to the fundamental cognitive functions of these children, such as adding training contents of intentional attention about the numbers in the curriculum for these children.
